title: FloodGuard AI
body: Next-season district flood-exposure estimation
M.Sohail 16032  |  M.Umar 16031
CUSIT · Programming for Artificial Intelligence · Fall 2026
note: Sohail, 30 seconds. Introduce the historical evaluation and say clearly that it is not a live warning system.

title: Problem and proposed stakeholder
body: District preparedness analysts need evidence about historical exposure.
Predict the next season’s flooded area percentage for known districts.
Targets: MAE ≤ 5 points and ≥ 10% improvement over persistence.
These are classroom targets, not operational acceptance criteria.
note: Sohail, 50 seconds. Context: World Bank 2022 PDNA, reference 2. No stakeholder interview or approval is claimed.

title: Dataset and audit
body: 640 records · 160 districts · four seasons (2022–2025)
District table selected; 2,308-row tehsil alternative compared.
No missing cells or duplicate district-year keys.
Public Zenodo source; CC BY 4.0; publisher checksums verified.
note: Sohail, 60 seconds. Sources 1 and 7 in REFERENCES.md. Explain why more tehsil rows do not add seasons.

title: Exploratory analysis
body: Many low percentages and a long upper tail.
Seasonal and regional differences favour temporal evaluation.
Four EDA figures use 2022–2024 only.
note: Sohail, 50 seconds. Explain skew and why a median benchmark matters. All plotted values are computed from bundled source data.

title: Features and evaluation design
body: Inputs: prior-season percentage, district area and province.
Exclude current-season flood measurements and spatial statistics.
Fit 2023 → select on 2024 → refit 2023–2024 → test 2025.
Same districts across years; unseen districts are not tested.
note: Umar, 60 seconds. Explain the exact lag join and training-only preprocessing. Sources 5 and 6; full method in pipeline.py.

title: Three experiments
body: E1: Ridge, prior-season percentage only.
E2: Ridge, add area and one-hot province.
E3: Random Forest, same expanded features.
2024 MAE: 4.020 / 4.096 / 4.006; forest selected.
note: Umar, 45 seconds. Forest wins by a tiny margin. Selection metric was fixed; no claim of statistically significant superiority.

title: Final holdout results
body: Forest: MAE 2.726 points · RMSE 6.016 · R² −0.978.
Persistence MAE: 4.388; training-median MAE: 2.474.
Beating persistence does not establish useful forecasting skill.
note: Umar, 60 seconds. Show all results, including the stronger median benchmark. Do not call MAE an accuracy percentage.

title: Working demo and reliability
body: python demo.py --district PK101 --year 2025
Display a real held-out prediction alongside the observation.
12 tests passed; nine notebook code cells executed.
Four seasons and uneven regional errors limit generalisation.
note: Umar, 90 seconds including demo. Use demo.py offline. Then show PK707 to demonstrate a large error rather than hiding it.

title: Recommendation and team follow-through
body: Keep the workflow as an auditable research baseline.
Add earlier seasons and weather/river predictors; validate again.
Sohail: proposed data/EDA review. Umar: proposed model/test review.
Actual contributions, team-size resolution and Git evidence remain pending.
note: Both, 45 seconds. No operational use. Source references and full attribution are in the accompanying report. Mention AI assistance and that proposed roles are not completed contributions.
